question.text: The mass of silver (Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Ag</mi><mo>:</mo><mn>108</mn><msup><mi>gmol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> ) displaced by a quantity of electricity which displaces <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5600</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> at S.T.P. will be _____ g.

solution.text:
Given Molar mass of Ag:108 gmol-1

Equal equivalents of substances deposited or liberated when some quantity of electricity passed through circuite in the electrolysis cell.

Equivalents of silver deposited= Equivalents of  O2 liberated.
Let x gm silver displaced,
(Molar volume of gas at STP =22.4L )

Number equivalents of a substance = The number of moles of substance × Valence factor of that substance
x×1108=5.622.4×4,x=108 gm.
